The probe worker returned this text when the harness refused it a report file; the coordinating session wrote it here unchanged on 2026-10-16. The worktree `/home/user/fortress-probe-where` holds the patches and the new tests.

# `where` clauses and the distance to the switch-over: a measurement

This is a measurement probe on the branch `wip/probe-where-clauses`, in the worktree `/home/user/fortress-probe-where`. The worktree was seeded from the base build `/home/user/fortress-base16` (`528438ac5`; `main` at `d731fc328` has changed no code since). The edits are uncommitted in the worktree; the patches are quoted inline below. There are two parts, written in this order and kept apart:

- **Part A** is the brief: library edits that use no new language, and what the code generator does with `NatParam`'s clause. Part A was finished and written before Part B began.
- **Part B** is the curator's addition, sent mid-task: the narrow `where`-clause forms, built as shadow patches in the compiled checker.

---

# Part A: library edits with no new language

## A.0 In short

| Group (ledger row) | Errors | Cause | Library edit that clears it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SUM`'s fusion pairs with `MAX` and `MIN` (433) | 6 | Four errors: `SumReduction` (bound `AdditiveGroup`) names `MaxReduction[\T\]`, `MinReduction[\T\]` and their pairs, whose bounds it does not meet. Two errors: the `distribute` overloads answer a pair over `Maybe[\T\]`, where the inherited `distribute` answers a pair over `T`. No bound fixes those two. | **Yes: removal.** Only the team's experimental `Generator2` reaches these declarations, and none of its answers change. A `where` clause would clear only 4 of the 6. |
| `AnyList`'s `\|\|`, `addLeft`, `addRight`, and the list comprehension's unwrap (636) | 4 | `AnyList` and `AnyCovColl` are supertraits with no element type. Their bodies call functions that need a `List[\E\]` or a `CovariantCollection[\T\]`. | **Yes.** `\|\|` moves into `List[\E\]` through one private generic helper. `addLeft`/`addRight` become `singleton(e) \|\| self`. The unwrap takes `cast[\CovariantCollection[\T\]\]`. Walk prints the same 14 lines on a probe before and after. |
| The identities' numeral fallback (436) | 2 | `else => 0` and `else => 1` answer a numeral where `T` is declared. | **Yes, for the checker:** `cast[\T\](0)` and `cast[\T\](1)`, the device the branches above already use. Row 436's own defect (an empty sum over a non-number group has no zero) stays. |
| `LexicographicOrder`'s `CMP` (634, list half) | 1 | `a CMP b` on values of the unbounded element type `E`. | **No.** Each device loses something the judgement on record weighed. Clearing it needs a list to be ordered exactly when its elements are: conditional extension. |

- **Distance with all three edits: 49 to 37.** Exactly the twelve sites above go, and none appear.
- **Walk:** all 621 tests of `ProjectFortress/tests`, run in one JVM, give 2 failures. The base fails the same two with the same seed, and both pass when run alone. One revival test, `GeneratorDeclarations.fss`, needed three lines changed. microGPT's quick pair passes 7 of 7 checks each.
- **The code generator on `NatParam`:** it refuses the trait at its guard, "Can't compile TraitDecl" (`CodeGen.java:5027-5033`). With only that guard relaxed in a scratch copy, a trait with a bindings-only clause compiles and runs. Opening a value at a call then fails the JVM's verifier.

## A.1 The thirteen errors, traced

# Part B: the narrow `where`-clause forms, as shadow patches in the checker

I built these by compiling the changed Scala and Java files with `scalac`/`javac` and copying the classes over the worktree's `ProjectFortress/build`. The originals are saved in `tmp/build-orig/classes.tar`. I did not use ant. The full checker diff is `tmp/partB-checker-final.patch` (353 lines). I wrote every test first and saw it fail on the unpatched checker.

## B.0 In short

| Form | Clears, with the team's spelling in the library | Soundness tests | Hole measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. A type variable in a `comprises` clause, opened at a call (`AnyList`) | `app(self,f)`: 1 of row 636's 4 | escape refused; two values not taken as one; the Amin–Tate shape refused | none in this form |
| 2. A `where` constraint read as a bound (row 677) | row 433's 4 `wellformed` errors; its 2 `return-type` errors stay, as A.1 predicted | calls with an unmet constraint on the function's own parameter are refused | a constraint on the enclosing trait's parameter is not checked at a dotted call |
| 3. Conditional extension, by the accepted rule | row 634's `CMP` | lists of numbers and of strings compare; a list of functions does not; a vector of numbers adds, a vector of strings does not | a member checked under the condition stays callable where the condition fails |
| 4. `HasIdentity` | not built: it needs a `coerces` constraint, a fourth kind of clause | — | — |

**Distance runs:**

- **All forms, with the team's spellings and no Part A edits: 49 to 43.** Six sites clear: 433's 4, 636's `app`, 634's `CMP`. Nothing new appears beyond two array errors whose union members swapped order. Still open: 433's 2 return-type errors, `addL`/`addR`, the comprehension, and 436's 2.
- **Part A plus only the form it could not avoid (conditional extension): 37 to 36.** `CMP` clears and nothing is new. So all thirteen are cleared by Part A plus conditional extension.

**Tests:**

- The compiler track (`CompilerJUTest` in one JVM): 1221 tests, 3 failures. These are the three red tests below that mark holes or a promotion. Every other test passes, including the `NatOpen*` tests.
- The library track: `OK (86 tests)`. The other-compiler track: `OK (263 tests)`. Both counts match batch 15b.
- Walk, on both Part B libraries: 19 where-clause, list and generator tests give `OK (19 tests)`.
- The whole walk folder on Part A plus conditional extension: 621 tests, the same 2 failures as the base.
- microGPT on Part A plus conditional extension: 7 of 7 each.

## B.1 A type variable opened from a `comprises` clause

**Lines changed** (worktree):

- `TypeDisambiguator.java:88-99, 111, 115-116, 120, 122`: a trait's `where`-bound type variables are in scope in its `comprises` clause, self type, parameters and members, but not in its extends clause. Without this, "E is undefined." The self type and the `self` parameters carry the comprised types.
- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:820-824`: `whereSizes` now includes type bindings.
- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:845-861`: `openWhereSizes` makes a fresh `E#k`, bounded by its binding's bounds at the trait's arguments.
- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:808, 911`: the arguments are passed through.
- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:307-312`: a comprising trait reached as a parent is not opened. Without this, List lost 22 sites to a second, wrong opening.
- `KindEnv.scala:79-81, 111-118`: a registry of opened names, found from every environment.
- `BuildEnvironments.java:954-962` (walk): a type `where` variable is bound as a symbolic type. Without it, walk stops at load with "Missing type E", then "Get of unset extends".

**Tests** (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests`, uncommitted):

- `OpenTypeChecker` (typecheck): before, "E is undefined."; after, `OK`.
- `XXXOpenTypeEscapeChecker`: after, "Function body has type E#7, but declared return type is ZZ32." and "Right-hand side has type Box[\E#25\], but declared type is Box[\ZZ32\]." The harness reports "Saw expected failure".
- `XXXOpenTypeTwoChecker`: after, "two ... is not applicable to an argument of type (AnyBox, AnyBox)". Expected.
- `XXXOpenTypeBoundEvidenceChecker`: after, "Could not check call to function upcast - [\A extends Object, T extends Object, B extends A\](Constrain[\A,T,B\], B)->A is not applicable to an argument of type (Witness[\U,T\], T)." Expected.

**Amin and Tate's shape.** Fortress can write it: `trait Witness[\A,T\] comprises { Constrain[\A,T,B\] } where [\B extends A\] { T extends B }`. The false evidence still never forms, for two reasons:

- Measured: an opened variable carries only its binding's own bound, not the constraint's lower bound.
- By reading, not tested: no value of `Witness[\U,T\]` can exist for unrelated `T` and `U`. Fortress has no null, and an object extending `Witness` must be a listed `Constrain[\U,T,B\]` for a `B` its own declaration names. That declaration's well-formedness is checked (`traits.tex:235-245`). My first attempt, which wrote the binding without `extends A`, was refused for exactly that ("B does not satisfy the corresponding bound A").

**In the library** (`List.fsi:56`, `List.fss:87` uncommented):

- `app(self,f)` clears.
- `addL`/`addR` stay, now on `(AnyList & {List[\E\]})`. Their element-type inference over `Any` fails as it does in Part A.
- The comprehension stays. `AnyCovColl` has no clause, and the opening applies to arguments, not to method receivers.

## B.2 A `where` constraint read as a bound (row 677)

**Lines changed:**

- `KindEnv.scala:48-49, 57-58, 136-153` (`constraintBounds`): inside a declaration, `X extends B` bounds `X`, whether `X` is the declaration's own parameter, a `where` variable, or an enclosing trait's parameter.
- `STypesUtil.scala:189-207`: a constraint on the function's own parameter is folded into its schema, so calls are checked against it.

**Tests:**

- `WhereBoundMethodChecker`: before, "No such method T.show."; after, `OK`.
- `XXXWhereBoundChecker` (row 677's gated reproducer): before, "No such method U.f." After, the checker accepts it and the code generator refuses: "Don't know how to compile this kind of FnDecl. node = g[\U extends Object\](u:U):String". It is red, ready for promotion to a code-generator `XXX` test.
- `XXXWhereBoundCallChecker` (red, the hole):
  - `g("s")` is refused: "[\U extends Object Shows\]U->String is not applicable to an argument of type String".
  - `Holder[\String\]("s").showIt()`, whose method constrains its trait's `T`, is accepted. Before the `STypesUtil` fold, both calls were accepted.

**In the library.** I added `where { T extends StandardMax[\T\] }` and `where { T extends StandardMin[\T\] }` to `SumReduction`'s overloads. The 4 `wellformed` errors clear and the 2 `return-type` errors stay. Walk runs `GeneratorDeclarations` with these clauses (green).

## B.3 Conditional extension, by the accepted rule

The rule: inside a declaration that extends a type under a `where` clause, the condition holds while its members are checked, and the subtyping itself is conditional.

**Lines changed:**

- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:872-896` (`isConditional`, `conditionalParents`): `parents` leaves out a parent whose clause has only constraints. A clause that binds new variables keeps today's reading.
- `TypeAnalyzer.scala:317-321`: a conditional parent counts as a parent exactly where its condition holds. The condition is a formula, so inference flows through it.
- `KindEnv.scala:120-134` (`withExtendsConditions`).
- `Decls.scala:87-88, 133-134`: members are checked with the condition holding.
- `TypeWellFormedChecker.scala:116-117, 127-128`: the extends clause is checked with the condition holding.

**Tests** (self-contained; `Num` stands in for `ZZ32`, because a test cannot make `ZZ32` extend its own trait):

- `CondExtendChecker`: before, 4 errors ("Ill-formed type: Ord[\E\] ...", "No such method E.lt."); after, `OK`.
- `XXXCondExtendRefuseChecker`: after, exactly 2 errors, on `(Lst[\Fn\], Lst[\Fn\])` and `(Vec[\String\], Vec[\String\])`.
- `XXXCondExtendMemberChecker` (red, the hole): `Lst[\Fn\](...).lt(...)` is accepted. Swift, Rust and Haskell avoid this by scoping such members to the condition.

**In the library:**

- `LexicographicOrder[\T ..., E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\]\]` in `FortressLibrary.fsi:1344` and `.fss:2058`.
- `List[\E\] extends { AnyList, ZeroIndexed[\E\], LexicographicOrder[...] where { E extends StandardTotalOrder[\E\] } }` in `List.fsi:67`, `List.fss:112`, and `PureList.fss:41`.

`ZeroIndexed[\E\]` must be written outside the condition. Without it the distance went from 49 to 71: List lost `|l|`, `generate` and `filter` wherever `E` is unconstrained, giving 22 new sites such as "operator |_| ... not applicable to an argument of type List.List[\E\]". This is the same point as the judgement's structural `=`.

Walk passes every test with these edits, including lists of tuples. So walk checks neither the new bound nor the condition, and its behaviour is unchanged.

## B.4 The empty `SUM`'s zero: does `HasIdentity` need a `where` clause?

In the specification's design, yes. Its one clause is `where { T coerces Identity[\ODOT\] }` (`algebraic-constraints.tex:774-797`). "Coercions, unlike methods, are not inherited" (`conversions-coercions.tex:244-247`), so a bound alone cannot promise every `T` a coercion from `Identity`. The design needs three things:

- a fourth kind of clause, a `coerces` constraint, which is not a bound;
- the checker carrying a trait's constraint on its self-type parameter to every `T` bounded by it;
- an `opr` static parameter.

I probed it with `tmp/probe/hi/HasIdentityProbe.fss`: `zeroOf[\T extends HasId[\T\]\](): T = Identity` gives "Function body has type Identity, but declared return type is T." The checker parses the clause and ignores it. I did not build it.

## B.5 What the code generator would then need (row 701)

- **Bindings-only clauses** (`NatParam`, `AnyList`): `forTraitDecl`'s guard (`CodeGen.java:5027`) relaxed. A.7 shows that suffices for the class.
- **Opening a value at a call:** a test of the value's class, then its type or size argument read off its run-time descriptor. The dispatcher already does this when it calls a generic arm through its closure table (`OverloadSet.java:1029-1068`). Today the code generator emits a direct call that fails verification (A.7).
- **Method `where` clauses:** the `forFnDecl` guard (`:2967`) lifted. For a constraint on the function's own parameter, nothing at run time. For one on the enclosing trait's parameter, nothing either, as long as the method's argument types already carry the bound, as `MaxReduction[\T\]` does.
- **Conditional extension:** the code generator never reads an extends-clause entry's `where` clause; it only prints it (`:215`). So it would make every `List` class implement `LexicographicOrder`, and a run-time type test of a list of functions would answer wrongly. The class loader, which builds each instantiation, would have to add that interface only where the condition holds at the instantiation's static arguments.
- **`HasIdentity`:** a statically chosen coercion from a `where` clause, which none of the paths has.

## B.6 Decisions, defects, hand-overs (Part B)

**Decisions** (no POSITIONS entry covers them):

- Type `where` variables are in scope in the whole trait body except its extends clause, per `trait-parameters.tex`'s "All static variables ... must occur ... as a where-clause variable" and its extends-clause rule.
- A comprising trait reached as a parent is not opened.
- Own-parameter constraints are checked at calls. Enclosing-parameter constraints are left unchecked: not built.
- Only constraint-only clauses are treated as conditional.
- `ZeroIndexed[\E\]` is written outside the condition.
- I built the shadows by copying classes into the build, not with ant (one JVM at a time).

**Defects / holes** (each shown by a red gated-style test):

- An enclosing-parameter constraint is not checked at a dotted call (`XXXWhereBoundCallChecker`).
- A member checked under the condition stays callable where the condition fails (`XXXCondExtendMemberChecker`).
- Row 677's reproducer now reaches the code generator's FnDecl refusal (`XXXWhereBoundChecker`).

**For FACTS.**

- With the team's spellings, the checker forms clear 6 of the 13 errors (distance 49 to 43).
- Conditional extension alone, added to Part A, clears the 13th (36, nothing new). It requires `List` to keep `ZeroIndexed` outside the condition.
- The opened type variable passes the escape, two-value and Amin–Tate tests.

**Command worked out.** `tmp/run-track.sh <Class> <label>` runs one testFast track's JUnit class in one JVM with `fastTrack`'s settings (private caches, `-Xmx768m -Xss32m`, `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, `JAVA_FLAGS=-Xmx4g -Xss64m`). Times: compiler 273 s, library 73 s, other-compiler 126 s.

**Questions for the curator.**

- Conditional extension's rule as accepted lets a member be called where the condition fails. Should such members be scoped to the condition, as Swift, Rust and Haskell do?
- Should a method's constraint on its trait's parameter be checked at calls (not built)?

**Worktree left at:** the Part A library plus conditional extension (`tmp/partA-CE-library.patch`), with all Part B checker patches in source and build. The other states are saved as `tmp/partA-library.patch` and `tmp/partB-library.patch`, and the new tests are untracked in `compiler_tests/`.

64:    T=explorations/coordinator/tools/facts-extract.sh
usage: facts-extract.sh [--check] [--part N] [--page-bytes N] [--root DIR] [--common] [QUERY ...]

Prints what the queries name, whole and in the order they are given; a rung's
briefing is one such command. Each piece comes under a line naming its file
and section. The output comes in parts of at most PAGE_BYTES (default 28000);
part 1 opens with the size of the whole output in bytes and estimated tokens,
then what was asked for, where it is and what was not found; each part says
whether there is a next one, and --part N prints part N.

QUERY is one of:
  F-87, P-48             the entry of that number in FACTS.md or POSITIONS.md
  F-87+                  the entry, then each entry it points to and each entry
                         that points to it, each once, one level
  history:F-87           the entry's blocks in FACTS-history.md or
                         POSITIONS-history.md, oldest first: the provenance line
                         of each change and the line it replaced
  TITLE                  the FACTS.md entry whose title holds TITLE: an entry's
                         title is its bold opening, or where it has none, its
                         opening words up to the first colon, semicolon or full
                         stop; when no current title holds it, the entry one of
                         whose former titles (in FACTS-history.md) does, with a
                         line saying it was retitled
  section:HEADING        every entry of the FACTS.md section whose heading holds HEADING
  index:WORDS            the INDEX.md lines that hold every one of WORDS (at most 10)
  ledger:ROW             row ROW of the gap ledger, whole, under its section and
                         the table's header
  ledger-find:WORDS      one line for each gap ledger row that holds every one of
                         WORDS: its number, its status and the first 150 characters
                         of its claim (at most 10, then how many more matched)
  positions:TITLE        the entry of POSITIONS.md whose bold title holds TITLE, as

## What came up in this run

### 1. The count 39 and the distance 49, site by site

**As declared.** The record expected the distance 49, or 48 if row 488's `:130` went with H, and the count 39, or 38 likewise (`coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md:29`, `:380`). The gate read `COUNT SAME   39, declared none` and `DISTANCE SAME   49` (`compile-ladder/climb-batch-16/gate/summary.txt:118-119`), with no kind, class, unit or crash row moved (`gate/distance.txt:2-25`).

**The count.** Its table equals 15b's line for line: every api 0, `#total 39`, `#locations 38`, `#crash none` (`gate/checker-count.txt`; the gate's result, `result.gate.checkerCount`). content.content:
## 0. In short

- **The full overloading check.** `OverloadingChecker`'s three loops were shadowed so that they admit every operator. The distance run then goes `DISTANCE UP 49 -> 249 (+200)`.
  - All 200 new errors come from the overloading check. They fall in 11 families, listed in the table of section 1.2.
  - String's four families are 40 of the 200.
  - EmptyString's `||` (row 611) is 1, and FlatString's api duplicate (row 726) is 2.
  - The subscripts are 125, the integer power `^` 16 (P1's subject), the arrays' and vectors' `+` and `-` 9, Number's `=` 4, and `|_|` 3.
  - Nothing is gone.
- **The export check.** It reads the same `isDeclaredName` (`ExportChecker.scala:275`). Admitting symbolic names there too adds 2 more export errors (total 251).
- **Walk's own meet check.** With symbolic operators admitted, it refuses the library at load at EmptyString's `||` alone.
  - One declaration on that meet clears it.
  - The whole walk folder then gives the base's verdicts, except that row 611's expected failure is refused at load as its keys name.
  - The ranges' half of row 611 is already repaired (`b872d65a1`).
- **Juxtaposition's device on the four families.** Three top-level operators per family, with the meet declared, clear the 40 pair errors under the full check.
  - The device clears none of the three sites on today's distance.
  - Alone it moves the two `asString` errors to the new top-level declarations: distance 48 with F.
- **The conversion.** The two `asString` sites are freed by the library's own conversion: `("" || a)` on the left, as juxtaposition's own body and `print` do, and `cast[\Object\]` at the bottom. This works with or without the device.
- **FlatString's export error.** It is freed by two lines of its api.
- **With all of them,** `DISTANCE DOWN 49 -> 46 (-3)`, exactly the three sites, with nothing new.
- **What walk sees under the device.** Programs reach the String component's objects' own `||` only through String's abstract `opr ||(self, b:String)`.
  - Moving that member to the top level either changes what kind of string every concatenation builds (JCp) or needs String's api to declare the objects' `||` (JC, 5 lines).
  - Keeping it (JH) is refused by the checker, whose meet must sit at the pair's self position (row 545).
- **What moves under walk.**
  - Any form of the device makes walk refuse at load a program that declares `||` on a trait that does not exclude String. This is seen in `XXXFunctionalMethodMeetOperator`, whose refusal message changes.
  - The conversion makes `(1,2) || "s"`, `() || "s"` and `() // "s"` print where today they stop.
  - Under the conversion a function or a 7-tuple raises `CastError` instead of `ProgramError`.
  - The team test `extendAny` stops with `CastError`, because an object declared `extends Any` is not an `Object` on either path (new defect, section 5).
- **What does not move.** microGPT's quick pair passes 7 of 7 each on JC. The 34 concatenating demos keep their exit codes and outputs, apart from timings, random draws and moved library lines.

### 2.2 The ways, as shadow patches

**F, FlatString's api (in every way below):**

```
-  object FlatString extends { String }
+  object FlatString extends { String, DelegatedIndexed[\Char, ZZ32\] }
-    opr ||(a:FlatString, self): String
```

### 2.6 The library's own way to turn any value into a string

- **The library's way.** It is concatenation with the empty string: `print(a:Any) = print("" a)`, "because the formulation with concat also works for tuples" (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4498-4501`). Juxtaposition's own `(a:Any, b:String)` is `(""||a) || b` (`:4462`).
- **Where the chain ends.** That chain ends in `||(self, b:Any)` (`:4398`), which calls `asString` on an `Any`: the same site. Tuples of 2 to 6 elements and `()` get there through String's more specific members (`:4387-4396`).
- **What reaches the bottom.** Only objects, functions and tuples of 7 or more elements reach the bottom. For it the library's devices are `assert`'s typecase on `Object` (`:306-316`) and `cast` (`:33-37`, which is that typecase with `throw CastError`). C, JC and JH use `cast[\Object\]`.
- **Functions.** Nothing in the library prints a function (row 374), and nothing here changes that.
- **Not taken, by reading.** Declaring the bottom at `Object` instead of `Any` would leave `"" || a` with `a: Any`, in `print`, juxtaposition and `|||`, with no applicable declaration. So the checker would refuse those bodies.

## 3. One question or two, and which part frees which site

They are two questions, and neither part frees a site of today's distance.

- **Part (a): when the check reads symbolic operators.** This decides whether the four families' shape is a site at all.
  - Today's checker never sees it, so on today's distance part (b) frees nothing.
  - Answered "now", part (a) adds 200 errors in 11 families. String's four are 40 of them; EmptyString's 1 and FlatString's 2 sit beside them.
  - The other 157 need devices of their own: the subscripts 125, `^` 16 (P1's ask), the arrays' and vectors' `+` and `-` 9, `=` 4 and `|_|` 3.
  - Part (b) answers 40 of the 200.
- **Part (b): the device.** Under the full check it frees the four families' 40 pair errors and nothing else. Its forms differ in what they cost:
  - **JC** needs 5 lines of String's api.
  - **JCp** changes the kind of string walk builds.
  - **JH** needs the checker's meet rule to accept a meet at another self position (row 545).
  - **Every form** makes walk refuse a program that declares `||`, `|||`, `//` or `///` as a functional method of a trait not excluding String.
- **The three sites.**
  - `FortressLibrary.fss:4397` and `:4398` are freed by the conversion (C), with or without the device. The device alone moves them.
  - `FlatString.fss:12` is freed by F, FlatString's two api lines. F's first line is also what frees row 726's pair under the full check. F's second line costs one full-check error (FlatString's `|_|`, as SubString's), which aligning String's api header with its component's would remove; that was not measured.
- **The order.** Part (b) matters only once part (a) is answered "check them". Part (a) does not depend on part (b).

/**
   *  Return the arrow type of the given Functional index.
   */
  def makeArrowFromFunctional(f: Functional, lifted: Boolean): Option[ArrowType] =
    makeArrowFromFunctional(f, lifted, false, None)

  def makeArrowFromFunctional(f: Functional, lifted: Boolean, omitSelf: Boolean, declarer: Option[TraitType]): Option[ArrowType] = f match {
    case f: DummyVariableFunction => Some(f.getArrowType())
    case _ =>
      val returnType = toOption(f.getReturnType).getOrElse(return None)
      val originalParams = toListFromImmutable(f.parameters)
      val keptParams = if (omitSelf)
                     f match { case fhst: HasSelfType =>
                                 if (fhst.selfPosition >= 0)
                                   (originalParams.take(fhst.selfPosition) ++
				    originalParams.drop(fhst.selfPosition + 1))
				 else originalParams }
                   else originalParams
      val params = keptParams.filterNot(p => NU.isVarargsParam(p)).map(p => NU.getParamType(p))
      val plainTypes = declarer match { case Some(x) => params :+ x; case None => params }
      // A varargs parameter is the domain's varargs type, after its plain types.
      val argType = keptParams.find(p => NU.isVarargsParam(p)) match {
        case Some(v) => NF.makeTupleType(NF.typeSpan, false, toJavaList(plainTypes), v.getVarargsType,
                                         toJavaList(List[KeywordType]()))
        case None => makeArgumentType(plainTypes)
      }
      val effect = NF.makeEffect(f.thrownTypes)
      val where = f match {
        case f: Constructor => f.where
        case _ => none[WhereClause]
      }
      val info = f match {
        case fhst: HasSelfType if fhst.selfType.isNone =>
          bug("No selfType on functional %s".format(f))
        case fhst: HasSelfType => 
          Some(SMethodInfo(fhst.selfType.get, fhst.selfPosition))
        case _ => None
      }
      val sparamsJava = getStaticParameters(f, lifted)
      Some(NF.makeArrowType(NF.typeSpan,
                            false,
                            argType,
                            returnType,
                            effect,
                            sparamsJava,
                            where,
                            info))
  }

  /**
   * Make a single argument type from a list of types.
   */
  def makeArgumentType(ts: List[Type]): Type = ts match {
    case Nil => Types.VOID
    case t :: Nil => t
    case _ =>
      val span1 = NU.getSpan(ts.head)
      val span2 = NU.getSpan(ts.last)
      NF.makeTupleType(NU.spanTwo(span1, span2), toJavaList(ts))
  }

1:# Writing a test
15:## A test program
36:## Where a test goes, and how it passes
70:## How `XXX` works
79:## How a defect is recorded
89:## The order: the test, its failure, the fix, the pass
101:## Writing an `XXX` test
118:## Promoting an `XXX` test
132:## Names, comments, citations
- In the compiled test folders, the `XXX` prefix of a `.test` file's name applies to every command that the file drives: each must fail. So a defect at run time, whose link succeeds, needs two `.test` files ("Writing an `XXX` test").
- An unmet `run_*` check makes a run test red, whatever the prefix.
- The harness reports any link or compile exception of a component whose name contains `XXX` as expected, whatever the `.test` file's name. Only an unmet key of that command makes it red.
- An `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key, whose program compiles, reports "Saw wrong failure", which is red.
- A green `XXX` test prints `Saw expected failure` or `OK Saw expected exception`.

## How a defect is recorded

Record every defect that you measure in one of three ways, and say in your report which:

1. Your change repairs it: an assertion in your plain gated test. It needs no `XXX` stage.
2. It is deferred, and the specification settles it: a gated `XXX` test that asserts the specification's answer. Write it in the change that measured the defect, even if a later change will repair it. A deferred defect of a program that the checker accepts and that then fails the JVM's verification (`VerifyError`), linkage or a range check at run time is one of these.
3. It is deferred, and the specification is silent or a conflict leaves it open (`exploring.md`): a test that asserts today's behaviour, and a row in the gap ledger (`records.md`). If no program can observe the defect, or no gated test can pass while it shows, as when walk crashes on the program, write the ledger row only. Its reproducer, the row's cell that names the test, is `none`, and its notes give the command and its output.

If your brief does not let you edit the original tree, say in your report which of the three the defect needs, and write a ledger row for it, whichever it needs. A probe that only measures and reports is an example. The change that next works there writes the test.

## The order: the test, its failure, the fix, the pass

1. Write the test, with a plain name. Write the essence of the defect as a clean, minimal program, not the shape in which a probe met it.
2. See the test fail through the harness (`harness-one.sh` or `junit.sh`, `tests-running.md`) on the base's code. Do this in a run that ends before you first build or compile your edit. Under walk, do it before you edit a library source that the test reads. If your tree already holds the fix, run the test through the harness on the old code, as `worktrees.md`, "Running the old code", says.
3. Make the fix. See the test pass in your last run after your last change of code.

The test needs no commit of its own. A test that comes with no fix, such as one that guards a behaviour that works today, has no failing run: see it pass through the harness.

In your report, quote two to five lines of the failing run, if there is one, and the passing line, each with its command. In an edit of the original tree, put every check into a gated test, never into a one-off script. A probe that only measures may use its own script. Assert a value with `assert` in an interpreter test. In a compiled test, assert it with `assert` (above), or print it and check it with a `run_out_equals` key. The harness checks both, so they are part of the suite's verdict.

An edit of prose in `Specification/` or `Documentation/` has no test. Check it as `specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", says.

## Writing an `XXX` test

In a compiled test folder, name the component `XXXName`, in its file `XXXName.fss` and in its `component` line.

- For a refusal at compile time, write one `XXX` compile test, with `compile` and `compile_err_contains=<the refusal's message>`.
- For a code-generator wall (`compiler.md`, "What the compiled path cannot compile yet"), write `XXXName.test` with `tests=XXXName`, `compile` and `compile_exception_contains=<text of the exception>`.
- For a program that compiles and fails at run time, write two `.test` files over the component:
  - `NameLink.test`, a plain name, with `tests=XXXName` and `link`. It is red if the link reports static errors, but green on an exception.
  - `XXXName.test`, with `tests=XXXName` and `run`, and no `link`. Its run uses the plain file's link, so run the two files in one call of `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`, the plain one first.
  - The program prints `REACHED` in `run()` before the part that fails. The `XXX` file checks it with `run_out_contains=REACHED`, or with `run_out_does_not_contain=REACHED` if the run dies before `run()` prints. Never use `run_out_contains=PASS`.
  - Example: `compiler_tests/XXXBoxDotSpellingsRungW.test` and `BoxDotSpellingsRungWLink.test`.

Show the first `XXX` test that your change adds, and only the first, working through the harness (`harness-one.sh`, `junit.sh` or `fortress junit`), from its place in a gated test folder. A direct compile and run does not show this. Run it twice:

the static arguments of a declaration with static parameters with coercion,

type parameter that is a parameter's whole type.
So where the declared type of a variable is wider than the type of its value,
or an argument's static type is \TYP{Any}, it may run a declaration at a

types.

It does the same where the arguments that fix a type parameter inside other
types, as the results of two function arguments do, have several minimal common
supertypes.
Neither holds of a type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter,
itself or another, or that is declared with several bounds that the interpreter

- F-53 **The distance to the switch-over is 49 errors and the checker count is 39, at the last landed gate.** The distance counts the checker's errors in the interpreter's library, led by the sized arrays (F-54). The count stops where the checker crashes or meets an error it cannot pass; since row 680's repair (F-233) nothing stops it, so its 39 are the `FortressLibrary` component's own errors, every api at 0. Both are reported, never red. An edit can move one error that it does not touch, `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:130` (row 737; F-232), so a lone move of that site does not show the edit's effect. By kind and by site, a rung's before (the `coordinator` skill, `references/batch.md`, "The checker count and the distance"): the last landed batch's `gate/distance.txt` and `compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`.
- F-54 **The gate classes the distance to the switch-over by root cause, and the sized arrays and the one-off body errors lead.** The `#class` rows of each gate's `distance.txt` hold the counts. No coercion into an arbitrary `I extends Integral[\I\]` can be declared, so a numeral where such an `I` is expected needs `x.zero` or `x.one`. Row 680's crash hid no error: with its repair (F-233) the component's check finds none in `Array3`, and the distance lost its crash row. With `StandardMinMax[\T\]` added to the array bound, the overloading check ran past 15 minutes when measured, before row 688's memo. Detail: `perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage.md` sections 2 and 3.4; `compile-ladder/rung-checker-bounds/REPORT.md` section 6.
- F-240 **The checker's count stage takes 82 s and its distance stage 217 s at the last landed gate, climb batch 16's.** At climb batch 15b's gate they took 325 s and 1,075 s; the solver's memos (F-235) make the difference, not load. Both ran beside other JVMs, and no idle run of the merged tree exists. Load can lengthen a stage more than twofold: rung S's tree took 574 s for the distance stage at load 5. So a time compares only with one taken beside like load. Source: the gate's result and `compile-ladder/climb-batch-16/gate/distance.txt`. Detail: `reviews/batch-16-review.md`, section 2.
- F-111 **The checker-count and distance stages read only the compiler's phases, so an edit to the test corpora, the texts or walk's evaluator and natives cannot move them.** Both stages run `Shell.compilerPhases` over `PhaseOrder.compilerPhaseOrder`, which reads no test, text or record. Outside `interpreter/`, only walk's own commands, the `ENVGEN` phase that only they run, exception field types and unused code name walk's evaluator, and only the library's strings name its natives. Detail: `coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`, "Rules weighed by what they cost against what they protect", item 5.

(** A %MapReduceReduction% takes an associative binary function %j% on
    arguments of type %R%, and the identity of that function %z%, and
    returns the corresponding reduction. **)
object MapReduceReduction[\R\](j:(R,R)->R, z:R) extends MonoidReduction[\R\]
    getter asString(): String = "mapReduceReduction"
    empty(): R = z
    join(a:R, b:R): R = (j)(a,b)
end

(** A %MIMapReduceReduction% takes an associative binary function %j% on
    arguments of type %R%, and the identity of that function %z%, and
    returns the corresponding reduction. **)
object MIMapReduceReduction[\R\](j:(Any,Any)->R, z:R) extends MonoidReduction[\Any\]
    getter asString():String="MIMapReduceReduction from embiggen"
    empty(): R = z
    join(a:Any, b:Any): R = (j)(a,b)
end

(** %embiggen% takes a type %T% and an operation (either an operator
    %OP% or binary function %f% on type %T%), along with the identity
    %z% of the operation, and returns a function suitable as the right-hand
    side of the definition of the corresponding BIG operator. **)

embiggen[\T,opr OP\](z:Any, g:(Reduction[\Any\],T->Any) -> Any) : T =

Neither implementation runs every set these rules allow.
The compiled type checker refuses more than the Return Type Rule where the more
specific declaration's parameter type is an object type, as in
\EXP{\VAR{ident}\llbracket{}T\rrbracket(x\COLON{}T)\COLON{}T} beside
\EXP{\VAR{ident}(x\COLON \TYP{Circle})\COLON \TYP{Circle}} where \TYP{Circle} is an
object (row~542); the compiled code generator fails on two declarations with
static parameters whose bounds differ, the pair the Return Type Rule allows in
\secref{overloading-static-params} among them, and on the example of the type
group's paper of 2019 that overloads a method over an array list and a list
(row~537); and the interpreter refuses at load two declarations with static
parameters of which no pair of parameter types excludes each other (row~159),
that example among them (row~539), except where a pair of their parameter types
excluded each other only as it read each declaration at one symbolic instance of
its static parameters, shared where both declare the same ones: such a pair it
reads on the two declared domains, each over its own instances, by these rules.
Jan's example is still not a valid overloading, its two declarations having the
same parameter type.
The compiled type checker applies the No Duplicates Rule as it is now stated:
it refuses two declarations whose parameter types, read over their instances,
are each a subtype of the other, ``There are multiple declarations of \VAR{dup}
with the same parameter type'', two functional methods among them wherever their
\KWD{self} parameters stand.
It reads the abstract functional methods that a trait or object provides as it
reads the abstract dotted ones, so that an abstract functional method beside a
concrete one with the same parameter type is among the pairs it refuses, which
only its code generator refused before, as a malformed overload set.
It checks no overloading of an operator whose name is not a word of capitals
(row~584 of the revival's gap ledger): two declarations of such an operator with
the same parameter type pass it, and only its code generator refuses them, as a
malformed overload set (row~726).
The interpreter refuses at load two declarations with static parameters whose
parameter types, each read over its own instances, are each a subtype of the
other, as \VAR{dup}'s are; it loads a declaration whose parameter types are its
static parameters beside one whose parameter types are their bounds, a plain one
(row~549) or one whose parameter types mention none of its static parameters
(row~742), and runs one of the two.
The compiled type checker and the interpreter both refuse two declarations with
static parameters whose parameter types exclude only together, through a static
argument that another parameter's type fixes (row~740), and the compiled type
checker refuses two pairs of declarations with static parameters that the
interpreter loads, one whose parameter types exclude through the one instance
of a supertype they share and one whose static parameters' bounds exclude each
other (row~741).
-----
identical static parameters and ignored them.
The rules stated are those of the type group's paper of 2011 (Allen, Hilburn,
Kilpatrick, Luchangco, Ryu, Chase, and Steele, ``Type Checking Modular Multiple
Dispatch with Parametric Polymorphism and Multiple Inheritance'', OOPSLA 2011),
which the compiled type checker applies, with its Return Type Rule checked over
every instance of the less specific declaration; the pair refused above has the
shape of that paper's own example, which the compiled path used to accept and
then fail to verify.
Neither implementation runs the pair allowed above today: the interpreter
refuses it at load, since it asks two declarations with static
parameters for a pair of parameter types that exclude each other (row~159 of the
revival's gap ledger), and the compiled code generator fails on it (row~537).
The compiled implementation adds one restriction that is not a rule of the
language.
When one declaration with static parameters is more specific than another that
declares as many static parameters of its own, the two must declare them of the

- P-27 **The library's own practice is the standard.** What microGPT invented goes into the standard library, in the library's own style. Whoever extends the library first studies how it does the same kind of thing, and follows that pattern; exclusion, for one, is all over it. He had to find the diagonal's override himself (P-88) because that study was skipped. No fix is designed from the specification alone or from a workaround on the user's side.
- P-29 **Walk's speed is irrelevant to every judgement of Fortress's performance.** Walk is hundreds of times slower than Python's interpreter. So no performance decision of any kind, and no edit of C4, the flat model program, for speed, until microGPT runs compiled. The gate never runs the two microGPT programs, too long-running to be tests: it compiles them and records the phase that each reaches. A run of them, once possible, goes to a stage that does not gate.
- P-42 **An unbounded type parameter's implicit bound is `Any`, not `Object`.** `Any` holds tuples, functions and `()`, which `Object` does not, and the library instantiates its generic containers at tuples, arrays indexed by pairs among them. The specification states the bound, with a callout that keeps the Working Draft's `Object`. The compile path's `Object` bound departs from it until the switch-over (row 412).

10	// briefing, reasons and checks equal to lists16.py's, one reason per key, checks a sub-list of the briefing; the
11	// three checker rungs' sections stating P-148 and the walk rung's naming no count run; no backtick or non-ASCII
12	// character in any string the agents read; no text asking a skeptic to see a failure again or a stage re-run without
13	// a code change (the coordinator skill's references/batch.md, "The workflow"); no LEDGER_FROM (the gather numbers
14	// rows through ledger.py); the record holding no copy of the block. Its last lines say whether the tracked script's
15	// block equals the generated one, and count the problems.
16	//   node check16.js [--write] [RECORD]      RECORD defaults to explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md
17	const fs = require('fs')
18	const cp = require('child_process')
19	const path = require('path')
20	const ROOT = process.env.FORTRESS_HOME || path.resolve(__dirname, '../../../..')
21	const HERE = process.env.OUT16 || path.join(ROOT, 'tmp')
22	const SRC = path.join(ROOT, 'explorations/coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.js')
23	const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
24	const WRITE = argv.includes('--write')
25	const REC = argv.filter(a => !a.startsWith('--'))[0] || path.join(ROOT, 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md')
26	const block = fs.readFileSync(path.join(HERE, 'manifest16.js'), 'utf8')
27	const orig = fs.readFileSync(SRC, 'utf8')
28	let bad = 0
29	const say = (ok, text) => { if (!ok) bad++; console.log((ok ? 'ok   ' : 'BAD  ') + text) }
30	
31	function bounds(text) {
32	  const ls = text.split('\n')
33	  const m = ls.findIndex(l => l.startsWith('// MANIFEST - the coordinator replaces'))
34	  if (m < 1 || !/^\/\/ =+$/.test(ls[m - 1])) throw new Error('no rule above the MANIFEST line')
35	  const e = ls.findIndex(l => l.startsWith('// =========================== END MANIFEST'))
36	  if (e < m) throw new Error('no END MANIFEST line after the MANIFEST line')
37	  return { ls, start: m - 1, end: e }
38	}
39	const o = bounds(orig)
40	const pre = o.ls.slice(0, o.start).join('\n'), post = o.ls.slice(o.end).join('\n')
41	const current = o.ls.slice(o.start, o.end).join('\n') + '\n'
42	const spliced = pre + '\n' + block + post
43	const out = path.join(HERE, 'wf-spliced-16.js')
44	fs.writeFileSync(out, spliced)
45	console.log('the script\'s MANIFEST block is lines ' + (o.start + 1) + ' to ' + o.end + ' of ' + o.ls.length + '; the generated block has ' + block.split('\n').length + ' lines')
46	say(spliced.startsWith(pre + '\n') && spliced.endsWith(post) && block.endsWith('\n') && !block.split('\n').some(l => l.startsWith('// =========================== END MANIFEST')), 'every line outside the block is byte-identical, and the block ends before END MANIFEST')
47	
48	for (const f of [SRC, out]) {
49	  const r = cp.spawnSync('node', ['--check', f], { encoding: 'utf8' })
50	  say(r.status === 0, 'node --check ' + path.basename(f) + ': exit ' + r.status + (r.status ? ' ' + r.stderr.trim().slice(0, 300) : ''))
51	}
52	const AsyncFunction = Object.getPrototypeOf(async function () {}).constructor
53	for (const [name, text] of [['original', orig], ['spliced', spliced]]) {
54	  try { new AsyncFunction('args', 'agent', 'pipeline', 'parallel', 'log', 'phase', 'budget', 'workflow', text.replace(/^export const meta/m, 'const meta')); say(true, 'the harness\'s parse: ' + name + ' accepted as an async function body, its export made const') }
55	  catch (e) { say(false, 'the harness\'s parse: ' + name + ' refused: ' + e.message) }
56	}
57	
58	// The block, evaluated with the script's load checks (const LOOKUP_TOOL ... const keysOf) and its scatter line.
59	const s = bounds(spliced)
60	const manifest = s.ls.slice(s.start, s.end).join('\n')
61	const vStart = s.ls.findIndex(l => l.startsWith('const LOOKUP_TOOL = '))
62	const vEnd = s.ls.findIndex(l => l.startsWith('const keysOf = '))
63	const validation = s.ls.slice(vStart, vEnd + 1).join('\n')
64	const scatter = s.ls.find(l => l.startsWith('const SCATTER = '))
65	let r = null
66	try {
67	  r = new Function("const TOOLS = 'explorations/coordinator/tools'\n" + manifest + '\n' + scatter + '\n' + validation +
68	    '\nreturn { BATCH, BATCH_RECORD, BRIEFING_LISTS, RUNGS, SCATTER, BATCH_INTRO, ledgerFrom: typeof LEDGER_FROM }')()
69	  say(true, 'the block passes the script\'s own load checks')
70	} catch (e) { say(false, 'the block fails the script\'s load checks: ' + e.message) }
71	
72	if (r) {
73	  const ids = r.RUNGS.map(x => x.id).join(', ')
74	  const order = r.RUNGS.slice().sort((a, b) => b.expectedMinutes - a.expectedMinutes).map(x => x.id).join('')
75	  console.log('batch ' + r.BATCH + ', rungs ' + ids + ', scatter ' + r.SCATTER.map(x => x.id).join('') + ', intro ' + r.BATCH_INTRO.length + ' characters')
76	  say(r.BATCH === '16' && r.BATCH_RECORD === 'explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-16.md' && r.BRIEFING_LISTS === 'explorations/compile-ladder/plan-16/manifest/lists16.py' && ids === 'S, H, K, W' && r.SCATTER.map(x => x.id).join('') === order && order === 'SWHK', 'batch 16, its record and lists, the rungs S, H, K, W and the scatter by expected minutes, W starting beside S')
77	  say(r.ledgerFrom === 'undefined', 'no LEDGER_FROM: the gather numbers the new rows through ledger.py')
78	  say(JSON.stringify(r.RUNGS.map(x => x.gateJoins)) === JSON.stringify([[], [], [], []]), 'no rung brings a gate step: testSpecData runs from the last landed summary')
79	  say(r.RUNGS.every(x => !x.landsOnlyWith && x.expectedCheckerCrash === undefined && Array.isArray(x.expectedMoves) && !x.expectedMoves.length), 'no rung declares landsOnlyWith, a crash or a ladder move')
80	  say(r.RUNGS.every(x => x.expectedCheckerCount === undefined), 'no rung declares a checker count: it stays 39 by reading, or 38 where H loses row 488\'s site')
81	
82	  // The record's section 3, rung by rung, as gen16.py reads it.
83	  const rec = fs.readFileSync(REC, 'utf8')
84	  const s3 = rec.slice(rec.indexOf('\n## 3. The rungs\n'), rec.indexOf('\n## 4. '))
85	  const asAscii = (t) => t.replace(/`/g, '').replace(/…/g, '...')
86	  function section(id) {
87	    const m = new RegExp('^### ' + id + '\\. .*$', 'm').exec(s3)
88	    if (!m) return null
89	    const rest = s3.slice(m.index + m[0].length)
90	    const nx = rest.search(/^### /m)
91	    return asAscii((nx < 0 ? rest : rest.slice(0, nx)).replace(/^\n+|\n+$/g, ''))
92	  }
93	  // lists16.py's briefings, reasons and checks.
94	  const py = cp.spawnSync('python3', ['-B', '-c', 'import json, sys; sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1]); from lists16 import LISTS, REASONS, IDS; ' +
95	    'print(json.dumps({r: {"briefing": LISTS[r][0], "checks": LISTS[r][1], "reasons": [x for _, x in REASONS[r]]} for r in IDS}))', __dirname], { encoding: 'utf8' })
96	  const lists = py.status === 0 ? JSON.parse(py.stdout) : null
97	  say(!!lists, 'lists16.py read' + (lists ? '' : ': ' + py.stderr.trim().slice(0, 300)))
98	  const rerun = /sees? it fail again|re-?run by the skeptic|skeptic re-?runs|run the stage yourself|skeptic rebuilds|re-anchor/i
99	  for (const x of r.RUNGS) {
100	    const want = section(x.id)
101	    say(want !== null && x.section === want, x.id + ': its section is the record\'s section 3 for ' + x.id + ' word for word (' + x.section.length + ' characters)')
102	    const l = lists && lists[x.id]
103	    say(!!l && JSON.stringify(x.briefing) === JSON.stringify(l.briefing) && JSON.stringify(x.checks) === JSON.stringify(l.checks) &&
104	      JSON.stringify(x.reasons) === JSON.stringify(l.reasons.map(asAscii)), x.id + ': briefing ' + x.briefing.length + ' keys, reasons ' + x.reasons.length + ', checks ' + x.checks.length + ', as lists16.py has them')
105	    say(x.checks.every(k => x.briefing.includes(k)), x.id + ': checks a sub-list of the briefing')
106	    say(x.branch === 'wip/' + x.slug && /^\/home\/user\/fortress-[a-z0-9-]+$/.test(x.path) && x.expectedMinutes > 0, x.id + ': ' + x.path + ' on ' + x.branch + ', ' + x.expectedMinutes + ' minutes')
107	    say(Array.isArray(x.pointsToReport) && x.pointsToReport.length > 0 && x.pointsToReport.every(p => typeof p === 'string' && p.trim()), x.id + ': ' + x.pointsToReport.length + ' points to report')
108	    const texts = [x.title, x.blurb, x.section].concat(x.pointsToReport, x.reasons, x.briefing)
109	    say(!texts.some(t => /[^\x00-\x7f`]/.test(t) || /`/.test(t)), x.id + ': no backtick or non-ASCII character')
110	    say(!texts.some(t => rerun.test(t)), x.id + ': nothing asks a skeptic to see a failure again, rebuild, re-run or re-anchor')
111	    if (['S', 'H', 'K'].includes(x.id)) say(/P-148/.test(x.section) && /count stage/.test(x.section), x.id + ': a checker rung, its section states P-148 and the count stage\'s runs')
112	    else say(/neither stage/.test(x.section) || /run neither/.test(x.section), x.id + ': a walk rung, its section says that neither stage runs')
113	  }
114	  say(!/[^\x00-\x7f]|`/.test(r.BATCH_INTRO) && !rerun.test(r.BATCH_INTRO), 'the intro: ASCII, no backtick, no re-run')
115	  const paths = r.RUNGS.map(x => x.path), slugs = r.RUNGS.map(x => x.slug)
116	  say(new Set(paths).size === paths.length && new Set(slugs).size === slugs.length, 'every rung has its own worktree and branch')
117	  say(!rec.includes('const RUNGS') && !rec.includes('_ENTRY = {') && rec.includes('gen16.py') && rec.includes('check16.js'), 'the record names gen16.py and check16.js and holds no copy of the block')
118	}
119	
120	const same = current === block
121	console.log((same ? 'the tracked script\'s block equals the generated one' : 'the tracked script\'s block differs from the generated one') + (WRITE ? '' : '; --write splices it'))
122	if (WRITE) {
123	  if (bad) console.log('not written: ' + bad + ' problem(s)')
124	  else if (same) console.log('nothing to write')
125	  else { fs.writeFileSync(SRC, spliced); console.log('wrote the block into ' + path.relative(ROOT, SRC)) }
126	}
127	console.log('problems: ' + bad)

# Committing and pushing

**scratch**
: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, probe programs, lists and private caches folders.

Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.

## What to commit

- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
- In a fresh clone, `.claude/worktrees/` and `.claude/agents/` show as untracked, because the lines of `.git/info/exclude` that hide them are not in the clone. Do not commit them.
- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, which is gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.

## How to commit

Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:

    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>

- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:

      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB

  If your brief gives another session line, use it.

## Pushing

Push after every commit, so that a lost container loses nothing.

- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.

- The three `String` sites: wait on row 743. The shadow is C plus F in `fortress-probe-strings`, 2 files +3 -4; that worktree currently holds way JC instead.

- Rows 714, 691 and 695: wait on a trace.

- A's size is my split of a worktree diff that mixes B.1, B.2 and B.3. Its shadow predates batch 16's `TypeAnalyzer.scala` (rung S's memos), so it must be re-based. Its two parts (B.1 and A.2.2) were never measured together.

- The worktrees `fortress-probe-distribute` and `fortress-probe-where` and the local branch `wip/probe-generic-distribute` must be kept until the batch lands.
